answer: Each identity adds one cedar-tagged point to an atlas containing three fixed reef beacons, then publishes a fresh triangulation of the whole map. Every triangle must include a reef core from its own numbered site, and a site certificate may appear only once per epoch. With m identity points plus three beacons, the triangulation has m+1 triangles, so k entrants require sum from m=1 to k of (m+1) = k(k+3)/2 distinct cores. Duplicate points are rejected, and cloned points cannot recycle certificates or share one physical core.
